newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields Namibia smelter out until Dec.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields Namibia smelter out until Dec.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd's Tsumeb Corporation Ltd's copper smelter will be out of commission for at least eight weeks, a company official said on Wednesday.
"We are looking at probably eight weeks. That is a bit of an optimistic view, I think," Gold Fields Namibia spokesman Dermot Whyte told Reuters by telephone from Namibia.
Tsumeb mines and smelters, owned by Goldfields of Namibia, have been shut down since August 23.

The company reached an agreement with the Mineworkers Union of Namibia last week ending a bitter six-week old strike which exploded into crisis last week after MUN members took control of the group's three mines -- Otjihase, Kombat and Tsumeb.
Whyte said production at the three mines would not start until the smelter could produce a final product.
"We won't start producing concentrates at the various mines until we know the copper smelter is ready to produce final products.
"And obviously when those mines will start producing concentrates is dependent on how long it takes to finish the copper smelter," he said.
Tsumeb Corp said earlier this month that the strike could cost it N$50-N$100 million.
Whyte said revenue losses due to the strike were running at N$1 million a day.
The strike cost the company some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.
TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from the Tsumeb mines.
Whyte said TCL was in the process of installing a new lead smelter at the Tsumeb property which would probably not be ready for the next six weeks.
He said the union and Tsumeb management had set up a joint committee to trash out details of leave and retrenchments.
"We have set up a joint committee...to identify who is going to go on leave now -- obviously there is no work -- and the retrenchments," he said.
The union and mine management negotiated a 10.5 percent wage increase and also reached agreement on a retrenchment package for employees who would no longer be employed by TCL.
